facts.text: Assumption was originally called Tacusah, a name that echoes its early French Canadian settlers.
The town’s deepest coal mine, abandoned in the 1930s, reached over 1,000 feet below surface, making it Illinois’ deepest.
In 1900, First National Bank of Assumption opened and remains the oldest continuously operating bank in Christian County, surviving the Great Depression.
The Assumption Historical Society, founded in 2003, preserves the town’s unique heritage, including the story of the 1940s oil rush.
Kemmerer Village, a private Presbyterian childcare agency, was established in 1914 after donor Philip Kemmerer willed 400 acres to orphans in 1884.
A railroad built in 1840 transformed Assumption from a sparsely settled area into a thriving community, prompting the first boarding house for railroad workers.
